title: CLAY COUNTY BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay County Board met Tuesday evening at the courthouse in Louisville and made quick work of a fairly light agenda.

In the absence of Board Chairman Joe Goodman, Vice-Chairman Barb McGrew called the meeting to order.  Also absent were members Troy Britton, Rodney Franklin, Jeremy Kohn and Terry Woodrow.  With no visitors seeking to address the body, they moved to approve the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes.

Janice Brooks presented the Claims Committee Report.  She went through the individual amounts which show Paid Claims totaling $4,339,293 and Unpaid Claims of $833,286.  Members approved the report unanimously.  The board then approved a resolution regarding the release closed session minutes.

Clay County Hospital President/CEO Bob Sellers presented the Hospital Report.  He noted this is Hospital Week and employees are being honored all week long with a variety of activities.  Sellers then asked the board to approve medical staff credentials which they promptly did.  He said a groundbreaking ceremony was planned for the construction of the new health department, but inclement weather cancelled the festivities.  The ceremony is rescheduled for May 21, from 4:00-6:00pm and he invited interested parties to attend.  With that in mind, he said construction is already getting underway with the first order of business being the building of a road to enable the removal of the existing buildings.  They are to be removed on Wednesday (today).  Sellers added that with health department workers moving to the hospital campus, CCH is having to relocate equipment and personnel.  EMS staff and equipment have moved into Dr. Kumar’s former building, while maintenance personnel will need a new climate-controlled space to house equipment, vehicles and other materials.  He said they intend to build a new maintenance building near the specialty clinic on the northeast side of the hospital campus.  He asked the board to approve the project, which carries a $669,215 price tag.  The contractor for the project is Akra Builders of Effingham, and they plan to begin construction in June with completion in October of November.  A motion was made to greenlight the project and it was approved unanimously by the 9 members present.

Lyn Waller with the Clay County Health Department presented the Board of Health Report in Administrator Jeff Workman’s absence.  Waller added to Bob Sellers announcement of it being Hospital Week by stating national Nurses Week just ended Tuesday, but Nurse Month continues through the end of May.  She also invited people to attend the groundbreaking for the new Clay County Health Department on May 21 at 4:00pm on the hospital campus.  Waller called attention to Board of Health Report by noting that Beyond the Bell is welcoming kids this summer who are looking for some excitement while school is out.  The health department’s Spring Resource Carnival just wrapped up last week and was deemed a success with 250 participants attending.  The next event will be in Fall and they believe it will be bigger than last week’s event.  Waller says the are still accepting Home Care referrals, just contact the health department to learn more.  She encouraged people to view the Board of Health Report to learn the facts about the WIC program and it has the information about the Back to School Clinics they’ll put on before school starts.

Next Kishon Prince with Magoo and Associates of Effingham spoke briefly and announced that he is getting married and while he will still help the county with their computer needs while working remotely, he introduced Jeremy Bookland who will handle most things for Clay County.  Bookland then proceeded to present the latest stats, with the company resolving 484 support requests.  New election related security applications were installed for the county clerk’s office and they prevented a cyber incident at the Probation Office from escalating and moved personnel to a more secure email host.  They also assisted the Clay County Tax Assessor with new software for dealing with the various taxing districts.  Bookland also spent time addressing the training of users for help in identifying malicious and phishing scheme emails.  Terry Hronec asked for more in-depth training in how spot these emails and Bookland said he would look into providing the training.  He also noted that in the future Magoo plans to look at recycling, password management and Uninterruptible Power Supply/Battery Backup.

Next, Lieutenant Jason Abner with the Clay County Sheriff’s Office presented the Sheriff’s Report in Sheriff Andy Myer’s Absence.  Vice-Chair Barb McGrew noted the county has received three bids for the 2016 Ford Interceptor.  Two bids were higher, but they came from outside of the county.  McGrew stated that a note from Sheriff Myers stated the office prefers the local bid, Dale’s Auto Salvage, because should it be needed, the old vehicle can be a source for parts.  Board Member Kelly Colclasure said he would favor a local business rather than someone from out of county.  The board agreed and approved the $250 offer from Dale’s Salvage.

Highway Engineer Darin Koelm presented his report and noted that he was there without wearing a neck brace, for the first time since September.  But he says his neck and back are still weak and he was tired.  He offered thanks to LeeAnn Stanford for all the help she has provided over the past several months.  Koelm said they have accepted delivery of their track hoe, and it is being used.  He also added that mowing season is at hand and they get at it very soon.

In Executive Finance, Tery Hronec asked members to approve the final payment for the Voltage Regulators for Mini Splits in the amount of $1,950, paid out of the Capital Expense Account.  The motion was approved unanimously.   Hronec then said while the board had approved the 3 percent pay increase for elected office holders at the previous meeting, they needed to approve a resolution stating that fact.  Hronec presented the resolution, a motion was made to approve it and the motion passed without dissent.

In the Vice-Chairman’s report, Barb McGrew said the board had received a thank you card from the family of Darin Koelm and wished him the best in his continued recovery.

title: HAVEN WINS
full_story:
The Illinois Farm Bureau Actively Engaged Student of the Month for May is Haven Cash.

The senior at North Clay High School is a content creator.  Her original podcast, called “Diggin’ Ag On Air,” is aimed at spreading more awareness about FFA and agriculture.  “My SAE has been in agricultural communications through FFA,” she said.  “I thought it would be a great addition to my projects, and it really was where I found my passion.”

It’s not her only podcast project, as she also lends her voice to the school’s Cardinal Chirp Podcast.  Her FFA career has been impactful, currently serving as both North Clay FFA chapter president and Section 23 FFA president.  “Haven embodies the type of future leader agriculture needs: hard working, dedicated, service-oriented and grounded in the values and purpose of agriculture,” said Katrina Van Dyke, North Clay FFA Advisor.

Through the Clay County CEO Program, Cash developed her own business called “The Growing Point”, which creates individual gardening kits for customers.  “There is no green thumb required, I will help you and I will walk you through it,” she explained.  “I’ve even created a Facebook group for every person that buys a box where they can ask questions and get insider information.”

In 4-H, Cash shows sheep at the Clay County 4-H Fair and serves in a leadership role on the Clay County 4-H Federation board.  Back at school, she devotes time and energy to the North Clay pep club, business club, and student council.  In addition, Cash is a student-athlete, competing all four years on the North Clay High School volleyball team as well as playing club volleyball.

“Networking is really important to me,” she said.  “You never know these people you meet, what they may do someday and what shoes they may find themselves in.”

Despite all her many commitments, Cash excels in the classroom, recently being recognized as an Illinois State Scholar.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The May 12th Xenia Village Board of Trustees Meeting opened with public comments from Alif Sherwani.  Mr. Sherwani a representative for Philips 66 Gas and Go shared with trustees’ plans for renovations and improvements to the former Knapps gas station in Xenia.  Knapps gas station closed suddenly in December of last year amid financial investigations by the IRS.  The property was purchased in January by Mr. Sherwani’s employer.  Sherwani shared with trustees that his goal was to bring better quality service to Xenia.  “We aren’t just here to take your money we also want to put money back into the community.  Sherwani also requested the board of trustees to approve a liquor license for the gas station.

Upon this request, Xenia Village Chief of Police advised village trustees to postpone the approval of the liquor license for one month.  Chief Burkett cited broken promises to the community as his reasoning for trustees to postpone approval of the liquor license.  “I believe you, I believe what you’re telling us.  However, I don’t want to see a situation where you get a liquor license, you sell alcohol and no further changes or improvements are made after that.  That station is an important source of revenue for the village and its image”

Galen Garrison was sworn in as the village’s Mayor.  Garrison opted to vacate his seat and vote as trustee.

Trustees discussed ordnance violation letters sent out the previous month as well as the state of a dilapidated property in the village.  The owner of this property remains unidentified following attempts by the village board of trustees to gather information owned to the owner to address the state of the property.

In Police business Chief Burkett shared that Kat Osterholtz with Clip and Tip Strays had contacted him to ask if the Village of Xenia would like to donate to her organization.  Clip and Tip Strays is a non-for-profit located in Flora.  The goal of the organization is to reduce the stray cat population in the area by catching, neutering or spaying the cats which they then rerelease.  Osterholtz and her organization recently identified 12 stray cat colonies within Louisville.

Trustees approved the Villages new water sewer and trash rates which will be reflected on residents’ Junes bills.  Also discussed was how the village should handle outstanding water bills.  Trustees opted to review village ordinance before making a decision.

Village Superintendent Travis Lewis discussed with trustee’s recent repairs to water lines the valve on a water line which services 147 residents.  Lewis also discussed the state of the Villages lift station which moves sewers through the village.

Trustees approved a bid of $13,065 for the installation of new gutters on the village hall as well as discussed options on how best to spend the insurance money to make repairs to the city hall ceilings and roof.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Clay County Sheriff Andy Myers presented his monthly activity report during Tuesday’s Clay County Board meeting.  In the Report for April, the Sheriff’s Office issued a total of 12 Traffic Citations, made 21 Criminal Arrests and served 32 various Civil Papers.  A total of 20,451 miles were driven by Sheriff’s personnel during the month.

33 persons were processed through the Clay County Jail during April.  There were 11 inmates in jail at the beginning of the month and 6 in jail at the end of the month.  The average daily jail population was 9.

Also, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office received a total of $2,458 during the month.  This includes:

The Sheriff’s Office handled approximately 446 complaints, 89 of which originated in Louisville and 85 in Clay City.  The Sheriff’s Office conducted 26 Criminal Investigations and 9 Accident Investigations during April.

title: CROP REPORT
full_story:
USDA’s May 12th crop production report unveiled the first look at 2026 corn and soybean balance sheets.  However, wheat estimates stole the market’s attention as the department estimated the smallest US crop in 54 years.  Fewer planted acres combined with declining yield expectations dropped the US wheat production estimate to 1.56 billion bushels, down 423 million from last year.

USDA pegged 2026 corn production at 15.9 billion bushels, down 6% from 2025, with an average yield of 183 bushels per acre.  Soybean production is expected to rise 4% from last year at 4.4 billion bushels with an average yield of 53 bushels per acre.

USDA’s latest crop progress and condition report released Monday showed 54% of corn was planted, in line with the five-year average pace, and 57% of soybeans were in the ground statewide, 10 points ahead of average.

There were 3.2 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending May 10th.  The average temperature was 56.5 degrees 3.8 degrees below average, precipitation averaged 1.13 inches, .16 below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 3% very short, 13% short, 67% adequate, and 17% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 18% short, 64% adequate, and 13% surplus.

Corn planted reached 54%, the same as the 5-year average. Corn emerged reached 30%, compared to the 5-year average of 23%.

Soybeans planted reached 57%, compared to the 5-year average of 47%.  Soybeans emerged reached 31%, compared to the 5-year average of 18%.

Winter wheat headed reached 73%, compared to the 5-year average of 53%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 2% very poor, 5% poor, 20% fair, 63% good, and 10% excellent.

title: LOTHER CHARGED
full_story:
Former South Central High School teacher Shane Lother was ordered held without bond after being formally charged in Marion County Court Monday with grooming a 15-year-old female student.

The charge states that Lother, a person holding a position of trust, authority or supervision in relation to the child victim knowingly engaged in a pattern of conduct that attempted to seduce, solicit, lure or entice the minor to engage in any unlawful sexual conduct by communicating with the victim in person and via electronic messages.

Judge Ericka Sanders ordered Lother detained after finding there was a great risk of harm to the alleged victim if Lother was released based on evidence found on the victim’s phone and being involved in an emotional relationship with an underage person.

The alleged victim’s father provided police with the victims phone.  Jefferson County Detective Justin Titzer, who conducted the investigation at the request of Kinmundy and Farina Police, located several deleted emails from Lother’s school email account and a deleted email from Lother.

Two of Lother’s former co-workers told Titzer they had observed inappropriate behavior between Lother and the girl.  Lother reportedly told one of them he was physically attracted to the juvenile and admitted driving to the girl’s home to have a private conversation with her.  The co-worker said she always found Lother and the alleged victim in close proximity to each other.

The other co-worker expressed concerns about Lother’s interaction with the girl during a recent school trip.

When Titzer obtained a search warrant for Lother’s phone on April 23rd, Lother reportedly said the girl had a crush on him.  He also acknowledged going to the girls home alone to speak with her about what others had seen.  Lother also said he talked to her about their relationship, saying there was a relationship/interaction that he ‘felt too, but they couldn’t because there are 100 different ways it ends badly.’

Titzer talked to the alleged victim on the same day.  She said she had deleted all of her emails with Lother after he told her people were getting the wrong idea and they needed to keep their distance.  When asked why she would delete the emails and notes of innocent conversations, the juvenile said the conversation was not innocent.  The juvenile noted she did not want to get Lother in trouble because he was her favorite teacher.  She said they were very careful with their communications.

Lother waived a preliminary hearing and formal arraignment.  A jury trial was set for July 13th.  He is due back in court June 3rd for his next pretrial hearing.

title: AVETT BROTHERS AT STATE FAIR
full_story:
The Illinois State Fair is bringing a night of heartfelt lyrics and high-energy folk rock to the Illinois Lottery Grandstand Stage, as four-time GRAMMY Award nominees The Avett Brothers perform on Thursday, August 20th.

Known for their raw emotion, tight harmonies, and genre-blending sound, The Avett Brothers have built a loyal following across the country.  Their 2009 major-label debut I and Love and You launched them into mainstream success, and they’ve continued that momentum with chart-topping releases including The Carpenter and Magpie and the Dandelion, both debuting in the top five on the Billboard 200.

The band’s 2016 album True Sadness marked a career milestone, debuting at #1 on Billboard’s Top Albums chart and earning two GRAMMY nominations.  The journey behind that album was captured in the acclaimed documentary May It Last: A Portrait of The Avett Brothers, co-directed by Judd Apatow and Michael Bonfiglio.

In recent years, the group has continued to evolve creatively.  Their 2019 album Closer Than Together featured the hit single “High Steppin’,” which reached #1 on the Americana Radio Singles chart.  During the pandemic, The Third Gleam debuted at #1 across multiple Billboard charts, with the single “Victory” also topping Americana radio.

In 2024, the band released The Avett Brothers, a self-titled project that reflects their organic songwriting process and continued artistic growth.  That same year, Swept Away, a Broadway musical inspired by their music, debuted to rave reviews, further showcasing their wide-reaching cultural impact.  Inducted into the North Carolina Music Hall of Fame and recipients of a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Americana Music Association, The Avett Brothers remain a driving force in modern American music.

“The Avett Brothers bring an energy and authenticity that will make this a can’t-miss night at the Illinois State Fair,” said Illinois State Fair Manager Rebecca Clark.

Tickets for The Avett Brothers will go on sale Saturday at 10 am via Ticketmaster.  Tier 3 tickets are $58; Tier 2 tickets are $63; Tier 1 tickets are $68; Track tickets are $73; and Blue Ribbon tickets are $123.  A $30 Pre-Show Party ticket is offered as an additional upgrade for all paid concerts.

Mark your calendars for the 2026 Illinois State Fair, August 13th through August 23rd in Springfield.
